messages:
maria: heads up — seeing SMART threshold flapping on nvme0 on a handful of GPU nodes in us-east1. Attach failures for preemptible jobs spiked at 09:12 UTC. Seems correlated with lots of tiny writes from the quantization cache after model warmup. :eyes:

maria: basic symptoms: attach fail, +20-50% io_util, nvme reported medium write amplification, SMART attr 202 crossing warn briefly.

sre-bot: [ALERT] nvme0.smart.warn (us-east1) — 6 hosts alerted, severity: high — https://mon/redwood/alerts/4582

raj: can you paste iostat/smartctl and the process list on one of the hosts?

maria: paste below from gpu-attach-12 (trimmed):
```
# iostat -x 1 3
Device:         rrqm/s wrqm/s   r/s   w/s  rsec/s  wsec/s avgrq-sz avgqu-sz await r_await w_await svctm  %util
nvme0n1         0.00 123.00  0.34 512.50   12.00  2048.00  4.00    2.45    3.8   0.9    4.8    0.10  78.50
```
```
# smartctl -A /dev/nvme0n1 | egrep 'ID|202|233|241' -A1
202 Lifetime_Host_Writes_GiB   0x0032   098   098   000    12456
233 Media_Error_Count         0x0032   100   100   000    0
241 Total_LBAs_Written        0x0032   097   097   000    145678901
```

maria: top offenders in process list were our quant-cache worker (python) and the model warmup job that does many mmap+write ops.

axel: hunch: quant-cache is doing many small 4K fsyncs after mapping; overlayfs + underlying flash leads to write amplification. We saw similar with shard cache but magnitude here is larger because warmup churns sequentially across many model files.

jin: options: 1) throttle/aggregate cache flushes (coalesce writes) 2) use dedicated pool for heavy quant workloads (predictable cost) 3) tune kernel writeback/coalescing knobs per pool. Tradeoffs: 1/3 cheaper but can raise tail latency; 2 reduces wear and tail but increases unit cost (dedicated GPUs).

maria: tried a local test toggling vm.dirty_writeback_centisecs -> increase from 100 to 500 (i.e., 1s -> 5s). Observed ~40% drop in small-writes/s and SMART stayed below warn during the test, but avg response tail (p50->p95) increased by ~120ms.

raj: can we do targeted kernel tunable only on preemptible pool nodes first? That keeps dedicated SLA nodes untouched.

axel: yeah — we can apply via nodepool labels + DaemonSet. I'll draft a rollout plan: canary 10 nodes in us-east1-gpu-preemptible, monitor iops and tail latency for 2h. If SMARTs stop flapping and tail is acceptable, ramp to 100%.

maria: created a short grafana snapshot for canary baseline: https://mon/redwood/g/quant-cache-canary

axel: opening PR with the DaemonSet change and the sysctl: https://github.com/redwood-infra/ops/pull/842 (canary -> then 4-step ramp).

oncall-luke: tagging oncall — I'll watch the preemptible attach queue for ~3h and will revert if we see attach regression.

jin: paste cost calc quick: routing 20% of quant workload to dedicated pool adds ~18% to GPU spend for those jobs but drops risk of attach failures and decreases read/write rate on ephemerals by ~55%.

maria: decision: proceed with axel's canary for kernel tunable + coalesce. If canary fails, fallback plan B = route heavy warmups to dedicated pool and add a short-lived aggregation layer in quant-cache.

raj: can someone add an incident tag and short postmortem template? I'll capture metrics.

maria: added incident-2026-03-21-quantcache-nvme to the tracker. Leaving thread open — will post results from canary run. :+1:

sre-bot: [ACK] Incident incident-2026-03-21-quantcache-nvme created by maria — severity: medium — assign: eng-infra
